title: legal redlines scratchpad - 3p vendor contract (inference / hosting)
content:
Quick scratchpad for vendor contract redlines (third-party inference/hosting). Notes to self + suggested language. Informal - will convert to redline later.

Context: vendor provides hosted inference for customers (model serving, telemetry, optional model uploads). Concern: data use, IP, liability, security, SLA. Vendor template leans in vendor-favor (broad rights to use data, low liability cap).

PRIMARY CLAUSES TO WATCH (high level):
- Data use / license: vendor wants broad perpetual rights to use Customer Data 'to provide and improve services' - push back hard.
- IP / Outputs: who owns model outputs and any fine-tuned models? vendor may claim rights to derivatives.
- Indemnity / liability cap: vendor cap often 1x fees or $100k - too low for inference (PII exposures). Need higher cap or carveouts for breaches.
- Confidentiality & security: encryption, KMS/HSM, audit rights, SOC2 / ISO / penetration testing, breach notice timelines.
- Subprocessors / subcontractors: need notice and objection period; list of approved subprocessors; flow-down obligations.
- Termination & data return: termination for convenience? data deletion/return timelines; post-termination access for migration.
- SLA / remedies: credits only vs actual termination rights on repeated misses; measurable SLOs (p99 latency, throughput) and credits formula.
- Export controls & compliance: model weights, restricted data.
- Benchmarking & confidentiality of performance numbers.

REDLINE / NEGOTIATION TALKING POINTS (concrete language suggestions):
1) Data usage / model training
- Vendor clause: "Customer Data may be used to provide, maintain, and improve the Services, including to train and improve Vendor models."
- Ask: delete or limit to "to provide and maintain the Services for the Customer". No model training / improvement with Customer Data without explicit opt-in.
- Alternative language: "Vendor will not use Customer Data to train, improve, or develop models or services used for other customers, or for Vendor's internal model development, except with Customer's prior written consent."
- If vendor insists on aggregated non-personally-identifiable learning, require: (a) strong anonymization definition, (b) audit right, (c) prohibition on use with generative models that could reproduce customer data.

2) Ownership of Outputs / Derivatives
- Vendor may claim rights to derivatives. Push for: "Customer owns all Customer Data and all Outputs. Vendor hereby assigns any rights it may have in Outputs to Customer."
- For jointly-created models (if vendor fine-tunes on Customer Data), require explicit license terms and clear IP carveouts.

3) Liability cap and carveouts
- Vendor template: cap = total fees paid in prior 12 months, exclude consequential only in narrow ways.
- Ask: increase to higher of (i) 2x fees paid in prior 12 months or (ii) $5,000,000 for enterprise deals.
- Critical carveouts (no cap): breach of confidentiality leading to PII exposure, willful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement - list these as exceptions to the cap.
- Also add express carveout for indemnity for third-party claims arising from vendor's negligence or security breach.

4) Indemnity / IP infringement
- Vendor to indemnify for (a) Vendor breach of representations (including security), (b) third-party IP infringement caused by Vendor's deliverables. Mutual indemnity ok for customer's use outside scope.
- Require control of defense but with customer's approval for settlements that admit liability or involve injunctive relief.

5) Security / Compliance / Audit
- Require SOC 2 Type II (or ISO 27001) attestation annually.
- Encryption: data at rest and in transit; customer-managed encryption keys (CMK/KMS) for sensitive customers (optional add-on).
- Breach notice: vendor must notify within 48 hours of detection, provide root cause and remediation plan, support notifications to regulators/customers.
- Audit right: limited audit every 12 months, or SOC2 report + supplementary questions. For high-risk customers, on-site audit or third-party auditor with NDA.

6) Subprocessors / Subcontractors
- Vendor must provide current list and notify 30 days before adding new subprocessors. Customer has right to object for regulatory reasons. All subprocessors must flow down security/confidentiality obligations.

7) SLA & Remedies
- Define measurable SLOs: availability (e.g., 99.9% monthly), p99 inference latency (for given model/size), job completion times for batch.
- Remedies: service credits escalating with consecutive misses; for repeated failures (e.g., 3+ months < SLA) allow termination for cause and pro-rated refund.
- Avoid 'credits only' as only remedy for severe outages that cause customer losses. For enterprise deals, include termination right for persistent breaches.

8) Termination / Data Return
- Termination for convenience: 30 days. Termination for cause: 30-day cure period (unless material breach like data leak).
- Data return: vendor to export and return all Customer Data and Outputs within 30 days post-termination and certify secure deletion of all copies within 60 days. If vendor uses backups, deletion within 120 days.
- Transitional support: optionally paid, define rates for export/migration support.

9) Confidentiality / Publicity / Benchmarking
- Ensure performance numbers and security details treated as confidential. Vendor shouldn't publish performance benchmarks referencing Customer or Customer Data without consent.

OTHER NOTES / TACTICS
- Use risk-based approach: for small deals accept stricter caps; for enterprise deals push for higher caps and stronger controls.
- If vendor is critical (only provider for feature) negotiate a 'most-favored' carveout: dedicated SLAs or Dedicated deployment with stronger guarantees.
- For hosted inference with model uploads: require contractual guarantee that vendor will not reuse uploaded models without consent; if vendor wants to host fine-tuning, require opt-in and pay-for-service model with explicit IP terms.
- Ask for periodic security reports and integration into our Console/observability for usage audit (token-level logs, who accessed which model).

REDLINE SNIPPETS (copyable):
- Data use: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data, including model inputs, prompts, or uploaded models, to train, improve, or develop machine learning models or services that are used for customers other than Customer, except with Customer's prior written consent."
- Liability cap: "Except for liability arising from gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or breach of confidentiality, the aggregate liability of Vendor shall be limited to the greater of (i) twice the fees paid by Customer to Vendor in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, or (ii) Five Million US Dollars (USD 5,000,000)."
- Breach notice: "Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and in any event within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of a Security Incident affecting Customer Data and shall provide regular updates until the incident is resolved."

QUESTIONS / TODOs for negotiation meeting
- What is our acceptable liability cap for strategic enterprise customers? set threshold $X.
- Which of our customers need CMK support by default (regulatory)?
- Confirm whether we require yearly pen test results or attestations only.
- Decide stance on model training: blanket prohibition vs limited anonymized learning with strict controls.

LINKS to internal guidance (for me):
- Contract Playbook: see linked Confluence (above) - playbook has fallback caps and standard language.
- Prior redlines: see legal-redlines-scratchpad-maya-patel-inference-contract.json (examples of successful language).

Notes to self: keep language simple, don't accept ambiguous 'anonymized' without definition, insist on measurable SLAs. Prepare two negotiation tracks: (A) Standard (self-serve) - accept tighter caps and no CMK; (B) Enterprise - negotiate higher caps, CMK, audit rights, and dedicated deployment options.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to redline when we decide final approach.
